title: Hold jobs on low disk after cleanup; default 10G minimum free
summary: Add a minimum-free-disk check (default 10G, a default in config.rs, athena.toml untouched) before dispatch and before the checks. On low space it runs cleanup of terminal and idle workspaces' target/; if still low, it holds the job as 'environment: low disk' and tells the user, without rejecting it. Audience: the user running drain. Re-running job 20261016-044847-hem1 is a separate follow-up after this lands.

defaults_applied.how: New disk tests, with cargo test, clippy and fmt required.
Criteria name tests that exercise cleanup, hold and resume.
Docs written for an outside reader, using 'the user'.
One focused change; the hem1 re-run is separate.
The check is done before dispatch and before the checks, which is the cause of the full-disk failures.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Deleting a closed job's target/ already landed in 173d12e; this change reuses that cleanup and adds the idle-workspace sweep if absent.
The minimum is a config.rs default applying when the setting is absent; athena.toml is not edited.
Free space is injectable (a trait or function parameter) so tests can simulate low disk.
Re-running job 20261016-044847-hem1 is done by Athena after landing, not as an edit here.
Docs and output say 'the user', never 'the operator'.
The exact file layout is a guess; likely homes are config.rs, drain.rs and run.rs.

acceptance_criteria.text: With free disk simulated below the minimum, a test shows cleanup runs before the job is dispatched and before the checks. Run `cargo test --locked` and check the new disk tests pass.

A test shows that when space is still low after cleanup, the job is held with status 'environment: low disk', is not rejected, and the user is told, with free and required amounts. Run `cargo test --locked`.
A test shows that once space is freed, verification goes ahead for the held job. Run `cargo test --locked`.
A test shows that the idle-workspace sweep removes target/ and leaves source files. Run `cargo test --locked`.

config.rs defines a minimum-free-disk default of 10G used when the setting is absent, and a test shows the default parses. athena.toml is unchanged. The docs name the setting and the 'environment: low disk' status.
The user can see from drain output and status that a held job shows the reason and the free and required amounts. Wording says 'the user', not 'the operator'.
`cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` is clean and `cargo fmt --all --check` passes.

out_of_scope: Re-implementing deletion of a closed job's target/ (landed in 173d12e)
Editing the planning pass of job 20261016-044847-hem1 in this change
departures: Slightly higher cost: the change spans the config, drain and run paths, and tests must simulate disk.
urgent_reason: Disk-full failures have already stalled verification, for example the rejected job 20261016-044847-hem1, so holding jobs avoids wasted failed attempts and redo work.
